Here’s a quick rundown of the long‑weekend dates that will occur in Canada in 2023.  (All dates are in the local time zone of the holiday’s location.)  

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Creates a long weekend? | Typical long‑weekend span |
|---------|-------------|------------------------|---------------------------|
| New Year’s Day | Sunday Jan 1 | Yes – the weekend is already long | Jan 1–2 |
| Family Day (Ontario, Manitoba, New Brunswick, Saskatchewan) | Monday Feb 20 | Yes | Feb 18–20 |
| Good Friday (most provinces) | Friday Apr 7 | Yes | Apr 7–9 |
| Victoria Day | Monday May 22 | Yes | May 20–22 |
| Canada Day | Saturday Jul 1 | Yes – the weekend is already long | Jul 1–2 |
| Labour Day | Monday Sep 4 | Yes | Sep 2–4 |
| Thanksgiving (Canada) | Monday Oct 9 | Yes | Oct 7–9 |
| Remembrance Day (observed in many provinces) | Monday Nov 11 | Yes | Nov 9–11 |
| Christmas Day | Monday Dec 25 | Yes | Dec 23–25 |
| Boxing Day | Tuesday Dec 26 | No (no extra day off) | — |

**Notes**

* Family Day is observed in several provinces on the third Monday of February; the date above is for Ontario, Manitoba, New Brunswick, and Saskatchewan.  
* Good Friday is a statutory holiday in most provinces, but not all.  
* Remembrance Day is a statutory holiday in many provinces, but not all.  
* The “typical long‑weekend span” column shows the Friday‑to‑Monday period that would be extended if the holiday falls on a Friday or Monday.  

Feel free to let me know if you’d like the list filtered for a specific province or if you need the dates in a different format!
